speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. You mentioned experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That shooting pain when eating sounds like a specific trigger for your ear; does the pain also occur when you chew on the left side of your jaw or your tongue? Also, have you noticed any fluid draining from your ear or any change in the sensation of your teeth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia secondary to post-tympanoplasty inflammation.
